risk.summary: Three internet-reachable entry points -- the debug console, the users endpoint, and the proxy route -- each chain into code execution or data theft, and the same service hardcodes both AWS and database credentials.

findings.title: PyYAML: command execution through python/object/apply constructor in FullLoader

explanation.what: PyYAML's `yaml.load` without `SafeLoader` deserializes arbitrary Python objects from YAML input.
explanation.why_it_matters: settings_loader.py reads YAML from disk; if that file path is ever attacker-influenced, this is direct code execution.
explanation.fix: Bump PyYAML to >=5.2 and use `yaml.safe_load` everywhere.

findings.title: PyYAML: incomplete fix for CVE-2020-1747

explanation.what: A second, related full_load code-execution flaw in the same PyYAML 5.1 release.
explanation.why_it_matters: Same exposure as the other PyYAML CVEs -- one dependency bump fixes all three.
explanation.fix: Bump PyYAML to >=5.4.

findings.title: PyYAML: arbitrary command execution through python/object/new when FullLoader is used

explanation.what: A third PyYAML 5.1 deserialization flaw via crafted YAML tags.
explanation.why_it_matters: Confirms this isn't a one-off -- the whole 5.1 line is unsafe to keep pinned.
explanation.fix: Bump PyYAML to >=5.3.1.

findings.title: AWS Access Key ID committed to source

explanation.what: A live-looking AWS access key ID is hardcoded in config.py.
explanation.why_it_matters: Anyone with filesystem or git-history access gets a working AWS credential half.
explanation.fix: Remove the key from source, rotate it in IAM, and load it from an environment variable.

findings.title: AWS Secret Access Key committed to source

explanation.what: The AWS secret access key paired with the access key above is hardcoded on the next line.
explanation.why_it_matters: Together with the access key ID, this is a complete, usable AWS credential sitting in version control.
explanation.fix: Rotate the credential immediately and load both values from a secrets manager or env vars.

findings.title: SQL injection via string-built query

explanation.what: routes/users.py builds a SQL query by string-formatting request data directly into it.
explanation.why_it_matters: This endpoint is reachable without authentication, so a single crafted request can read or alter arbitrary rows.
explanation.fix: Switch to parameterized queries (`cursor.execute(query, params)`) or the ORM.

explanation.fix: Upgrade jinja2 to 2.10.1.

findings.title: Image user should not be 'root'

explanation.what: The Dockerfile never sets a USER instruction, so the container runs as root by default.
explanation.why_it_matters: Any code-execution bug elsewhere in the app now runs as root inside the container, widening its blast radius.
explanation.fix: Add `USER appuser` (a non-root user created earlier in the Dockerfile) before the CMD.

findings.title: Dockerfile does not drop to a non-root USER

explanation.what: Semgrep independently confirms the Dockerfile has no USER instruction.
explanation.why_it_matters: Same root-in-container risk Trivy flagged -- confirmed by a second scanner.
explanation.fix: Add a non-root USER instruction before CMD.

findings.title: Flask app running with debug=True

explanation.what: Flask's `debug=True` leaves the interactive Werkzeug debugger reachable.
explanation.why_it_matters: The Werkzeug debugger accepts arbitrary Python expressions -- reaching it is remote code execution, not just an info leak.
explanation.fix: Set debug=False and drive debug mode from an environment variable that defaults to off.

findings.title: MD5 used to hash passwords

explanation.what: User passwords are hashed with MD5 instead of a slow, salted KDF.
explanation.why_it_matters: If the user database is ever read, every password hash can be cracked in bulk with commodity hardware.
explanation.fix: Rehash with `hashlib.scrypt` or bcrypt, migrating existing hashes on next login.

findings.title: Server-side request forgery in proxy handler

explanation.what: routes/proxy.py forwards a user-supplied URL directly into an outbound request.
explanation.why_it_matters: An attacker can make the server issue requests to internal-only services (metadata endpoints, internal APIs) that aren't reachable from outside.
explanation.fix: Validate the target host/scheme against an allowlist before making the request.

findings.title: subprocess call with shell=True (line 23)

explanation.what: services/backup.py invokes subprocess with shell=True on a constructed command string.
explanation.why_it_matters: If any part of that command string is influenced by user or config input, this is OS command injection.
explanation.fix: Call subprocess with a list of arguments and shell=False.

findings.title: subprocess call with shell=True (line 32)

explanation.what: services/backup.py invokes subprocess with shell=True on a constructed command string.
explanation.why_it_matters: If any part of that command string is influenced by user or config input, this is OS command injection.
explanation.fix: Call subprocess with a list of arguments and shell=False.

findings.title: subprocess call with shell=True (line 52)

explanation.what: services/backup.py invokes subprocess with shell=True on a constructed command string.

findings.title: Untrusted data passed to pickle.loads

explanation.what: services/cache.py unpickles cached data without verifying its origin.
explanation.why_it_matters: Pickle deserialization of attacker-reachable data is a direct path to code execution inside the process.
explanation.fix: Switch the cache serialization format to JSON.

findings.title: TLS certificate verification disabled

explanation.what: services/notifications.py makes an HTTPS request with verify=False.
explanation.why_it_matters: This disables TLS certificate checking, so outbound notification traffic is vulnerable to interception.
explanation.fix: Remove verify=False and, if a custom CA is needed, pass its bundle path instead.

attack_paths.title: Debug console to AWS credential theft
attack_paths.narrative: An attacker reaches the exposed Werkzeug debugger left on by debug=True and runs arbitrary Python in the app process. From there they trigger the backup service's shell=True subprocess call to execute OS commands, then read the hardcoded AWS credentials out of config.py.

steps.label: shell=True subprocess call escalates to OS commands
Hardcoded AWS key read from disk

attack_paths.title: Unauthenticated SQL injection to credential cracking
attack_paths.narrative: The unauthenticated users endpoint is vulnerable to SQL injection, letting an attacker dump the full user table. Because passwords are hashed with MD5 rather than a slow KDF, the dumped hashes can be cracked in bulk, handing the attacker working account credentials.

attack_paths.title: SSRF into internal cache to code execution
attack_paths.narrative: The public proxy endpoint's SSRF flaw lets an attacker reach the internal cache service directly. By writing a crafted pickle payload into that cache, the attacker gets code execution when it's later unpickled, and from there reads the AWS secret key hardcoded in config.py.

steps.label: Malicious pickle payload executes on unpickle
AWS secret key read from disk
